claims.text: Structural and chemical stability in high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature is governed by a dynamic equilibrium between atomic diffusion and lattice strain.
The proposed dynamic equilibrium can be directly observed using in-situ TEM or XRD.
The initial high-entropy nanoalloys have a uniform distribution of elements.
High-temperature exposure affects atomic diffusion and lattice strain.
The interaction between atomic diffusion and lattice strain determines whether the nanoalloy remains stable or becomes unstable.
High-entropy nanoalloys will have greater structural and chemical stability than binary or ternary alloys under comparable high-temperature conditions.
The enhanced stability of high-entropy nanoalloys will be characterized by a lower atomic diffusion rate.
The enhanced stability of high-entropy nanoalloys will be characterized by a lower lattice-strain relaxation rate.
The prediction applies from 500°C to 1000°C and over durations ranging from seconds to hours.
Grain size and phase composition can be used as stability metrics.
